_doc: The curated target list for the daily comment drafts (owner 2026-10-28; studio/engage.py `load_curated`, `bin/studio engage targets`): per live character, real Instagram creators in his niche that post often and draw engagement, each with a one-line note on why it fits. `engage targets` lists the stored hits first (studio.hits, today nearly empty: the hits job has had no ScrapeCreators credits since 11 Oct), then this list in the order written here, at most 5 a day, skipping every handle drafted for that character in the last 7 days; a target from this list has followers, url and caption null, so the daily run looks its post up with `keyword_posts` or falls back to the profile link https://www.instagram.com/<handle>/. Handles are written without @ and without spaces, once per character (case does not matter); the file is refused with every problem listed for an unknown character, a handle with @ or a space, a duplicate or a missing note. Keep creators only: no news outlets, no brands or shops, no accounts centred on children. Filled 2026-10-28 from the social-data tool `keyword_posts` (network instagram, last month, limit 50) on each character's `hits.keywords` in scan.json plus niche keywords (Franz: dachshund, sausage dog, wiener dog, doxie, dackel, dog dance, funny dog; Reginald: butler, british humour, british comedy, deadpan, ukcomedy, dance trend; Lenny: office humor, corporate comedy, corporate humor, boss, manager, worklife, dance challenge): only handles the tool returned are here, the follower and engagement numbers in the notes are the ones it showed on the post it returned (Instagram's own counts, not checked), and an account the tool showed without a follower count has none noted. The tool returns four or so posts a call in limited-data mode, so the lists are what that thin sample gave; at 5 comments a day and a 7-day no-repeat rule a list of 20 lasts 4 days, so add handles (or use `engage targets -n 3`) before it runs dry. Order = priority: the first handles of a list are used first.
